title: Project Cybersyn
summary: Stafford Beer's team built a real-time economic feedback network for Salvador Allende's government using the Viable System Model, telex machines, and an operations room.
lesson: Cybernetic governance can move information and authority closer to where work happens. It also shows how quickly politics overtakes design.
note: Ended by the 1973 coup. Historians still debate how much it worked as intended.

title: Risk Assessment and Horizon Scanning
summary: Singapore's government built a national horizon-scanning program informed by Cynefin and narrative sensemaking to detect weak signals early.
lesson: Sensemaking methods can be institutionalized inside a state, but they need continual protection from reverting to prediction.
note: Later commentary asks how much of the original ambition survived.

sources.t: The Cynefin Co: Seeing the Invisible
Integrating foresight into policy: RAHS in Singapore

title: Buurtzorg neighbourhood nursing
summary: Home care delivered by small self-managing nurse teams with minimal overhead and no middle management, scaling to thousands of nurses.
lesson: Distributed authority can scale when support functions serve teams instead of managing them.
note: Results depend on Dutch funding rules and professional nursing culture; transplants elsewhere have been mixed.

title: Amsterdam City Doughnut
summary: The city adopted a Doughnut portrait to guide its circular economy strategy, asking how the city can thrive within planetary and social boundaries.
lesson: A shared picture of the goal can realign many departments without a single master plan.
note: Researchers question how far it has changed core economic decisions.

sources.t: TIME: Amsterdam is embracing a new economic theory

title: Participatory budgeting
summary: Residents deliberated and voted on a share of the city's capital budget through neighborhood and thematic assemblies, and the model spread worldwide.
lesson: Real decision power, not consultation, draws people in. Participation shifted spending toward poorer neighborhoods.
note: Weakened by later administrations; recent research documents its dismantling in its birthplace.

sources.t: WRI: Porto Alegre and the challenge of sustaining transformative change

title: Child nutrition through positive deviance
summary: Jerry and Monique Sternin worked with villages to find poor families whose children were well nourished, then helped others adopt their feeding practices.
lesson: Solutions already present in a community spread faster than imported ones, because they come from peers.

title: 100,000 Lives Campaign
summary: IHI enrolled thousands of hospitals in six evidence-based changes, using improvement cycles and peer networks to spread them.
lesson: A campaign structure plus local PDSA testing can spread practice fast across independent organizations.
note: Its headline lives-saved figure was challenged by researchers, and IHI published a reply.

sources.t: IHI: 100,000 Lives Campaign ten years later
The 100,000 Lives Campaign: a scientific and policy review (PubMed)

title: Menominee Forest
summary: The Menominee Nation has managed its forest on a sustained-yield basis for generations, harvesting while the standing timber has grown.
lesson: Long-horizon stewardship rooted in relationship with land can outperform short-cycle management on both ecology and livelihood.

sources.t: Menominee Tribal Enterprises: sustainable forest management

title: Student Volunteer Army
summary: After the Canterbury earthquakes, students self-organized thousands of volunteers to clear liquefaction silt, then became a lasting emergency response organization.
lesson: Spontaneous volunteers become an asset when officials make room for them and when light structure forms quickly.

sources.t: A shovel or a shopping cart: ten years of the SVA (PMC)

title: Plymouth Alliance for Complex Needs
summary: The council and health commissioners replaced competing service contracts with a single alliance of providers sharing budget and responsibility for people with complex needs.
lesson: Contract form shapes behavior. Alliance commissioning lets providers learn together instead of competing over targets.

sources.t: Co-operative Councils Innovation Network case study

title: Human Learning Systems in practice
summary: Dozens of public service organizations documenting their shift from targets and payment by results toward learning, relationships, and system stewardship.
lesson: The shift is less about a new tool than about changing funding, accountability, and management at the same time.

sources.t: JRF: relational public service can tackle hardship

title: Legible Practises
summary: A free book of six stories, collected by Helsinki Design Lab, about public institutions that changed how they work and the stewardship craft behind it.
lesson: Stewardship is a craft that can be described and taught when practitioners make their decisions visible.

title: Water shortage in Ojai
summary: Carnegie Mellon's transition design team worked with residents and stakeholders to map a wicked water problem and seed interventions across timescales.
lesson: Mapping a problem with the people inside it, across long horizons, reveals where small interventions can connect.

sources.t: Words into action: transition design in Ojai (SciELO)

title: Handelsbanken and Equinor without annual budgets
summary: Two large firms dropped fixed annual budgets for rolling forecasts, relative targets, and local authority.
lesson: Budget processes are a governance structure; changing them changes what people are allowed to learn.

sources.t: Forbes: how Equinor and Handelsbanken abolished budgeting

title: Highlander Folk School and the civil rights movement
summary: Workshops where ordinary people analyzed their own situations trained labor organizers and civil rights leaders, including Rosa Parks and Septima Clark's citizenship schools.
lesson: Popular education builds the analysis and relationships that movements later act on.

sources.t: How Myles Horton built a social movement institution

title: Haier's RenDanHeYi
summary: The appliance maker broke itself into thousands of microenterprises that contract with each other and serve users directly.
lesson: Large organizations can shrink the distance between decisions and users by dissolving middle layers.
